newsitem.title: UK: MCI, British Telecom take Portugal Telecom stake.
newsitem.headline: MCI, British Telecom take Portugal Telecom stake.

text.p: MCI Communications Corp. and British Telecom are taking stakes in Portugal Telecom SA, strengthening their operations in Latin America and fanning speculation that another deal with Telefonica de Espana was in the works.
Portugal Telecom, which already is in a joint venture with Brazil's state-controlled Telebras, said Monday that British Telecom will take a 1 percent stake and MCI a 0.5 percent stake in the company.

British Telecom and MCI said the deal was aimed principally at strengthening their operations in Latin America. British Telecom and MCI have agreed to merge into a global telecommunications giant to be called Concert.

Speculation about a possible deal between MCI and Telefonica de Espana was heightened by Portugal Telecom's English-language news release announcing the BT-MCI link. The release included a reference to a Pan American joint venture to be "announced ... by MCI and Telefonica Internacional."
Telefonica Internacional is a unit of Telefonica de Espana.
However, Telefonica and MCI denied that they had reached an agreement and said the announcement by Portugal Telecom was made in error.

Telefonica de Espana -- which in the last decade has built itself into Latin America's biggest foreign telecommunications provider -- said it was still in talks with AT&T Corp., as well as with MCI and BT.

Telefonica has been in talks with U.S. telephone companies aimed at forming an international alliance for weeks, and MCI was considered a strong possibility. Other suitors included GTE Corp., SBC Corp., the parent of Southwestern Bell, and Bell Atlantic Corp., company officials said last month.
Telefonica said Thursday it expected to name its U.S. partner soon.
Analysts gave high marks to the British Telecom-MCI link with Portugal Telecom. Portugal Telecom's shares were higher in trading on the Lisbon stock exchange.
Although Portugal is only a small telecommunications market, Concert will gain from Portugal Telecom's strategic position linking Europe and Latin America, analysts say.

"We are delighted with the outcome of the process," said Portugal Telecom Chairman Francisco Murteira Nabo. "(We) will work together to create additional business opportunities worldwide and particularly in Brazil," he said.
"Portugal Telecom is an ideal strategic partner for MCI and BT," MCI said in a statement issued by Portugal Telecom.

Latin America has big growth potential. The region has emerged from recession far faster than expected with growth of more than 3 percent in 1996, well above the 1995 crisis level of less than 1 percent, the Inter-American Development Bank said last month.

The stocks of Latin American telephone companies began surging on Wall Street early in the year as investors, who fled the region's markets after Mexico's fiscal collapse in late 1994, returned in force.
Analysts said the region's growth rate, coupled with the enormous room for expansion in the underserved market, made stocks in Latin American telecommunications companies seem underpriced.
